study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Zabihi et al., Biological Psychiatry: Cognitive Neuroscience and Neuroimaging, 2019
study_identification_part.si4_title: Dissecting the Heterogeneous Cortical Anatomy of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Normative Models

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract and introduction clearly state the objective to use normative modeling to dissect neuroanatomical heterogeneity in ASD by mapping individual deviations from typical cortical development, moving beyond case–control comparisons. The purpose is articulated as understanding heterogeneity and informing precision medicine, with hypotheses/questions centered on mapping deviations and relating them to symptoms.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "we used an innovative normative modeling approach to parse biological heterogeneity in ASD... we aimed to dissect the neuroanatomy of ASD by mapping the deviations from a typical pattern of neuroanatomical development at the level of the individual"; "Our main goals were to ... map the neuroanatomical features by which each individual ASD participant differs from the expected TD pattern ... and thereby demonstrate the value of normative modeling techniques for understanding the biological heterogeneity of ASD."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study built a new normative model using TD participants from the LEAP cohort. Eligibility/QC are partly described: included all LEAP participants with MRI scans surviving quality control; scans with severe artifacts were excluded after visual assessment by at least 3 raters; no manual edits allowed. Final sample sizes are reported (TD n=206). However, detailed inclusion/exclusion criteria specific to the TD reference cohort beyond general LEAP exclusions are limited, and reasons for exclusion are not fully enumerated.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "we included all participants from the Longitudinal European Autism Project (LEAP) cohort with a structural magnetic resonance imaging scan surviving quality control"; "We excluded a small number of scans with severe artifacts (e.g. caused by head motion). The rest of the scans were included 'as is'... Prior to analysis, all surface reconstructions were visually assessed ... by at least 3 independent raters."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and gender were used as covariates in the normative model. Given multi-site data, site effects were addressed by re-estimating models including site dummy variables; IQ and Euler number were also examined as covariates in sensitivity analyses, with conclusions unchanged.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "training a Gaussian process regression model on the TD cohort ... using age and gender as covariates"; "we estimated a separate normative model additionally including dummy regressors for IQ, site, and FreeSurfer Euler number"; "re-estimated after additionally including IQ and scanning site dummy variables and FreeSurfer Euler number as covariates ... differences ... negligible"

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The reference cohort comprises typically developing participants from the LEAP (Longitudinal European Autism Project), a large international multi-site study with harmonized acquisition procedures. Recruitment and cohort structure are described.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "we included all participants from the Longitudinal European Autism Project (LEAP) cohort ..."; "we employed data from a large international study ... with harmonized data acquisition procedures"

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Primary MRI acquisition is described at a high level: T1-weighted images acquired using a standard ADNI sequence matched across sites. However, detailed acquisition parameters (e.g., TR/TE, resolution) and equipment specifications (manufacturer, field strength) are not provided in the available text.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: "A high resolution T1-weighted image was acquired from each participant with a standard Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) sequence, matched across scanning sites."

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing is clearly described: cortical thickness estimated with FreeSurfer v5.3; surfaces visually QC'd by at least three raters; scans with severe artifacts excluded; no manual edits; surface-based smoothing with 10-mm kernel.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "Cortical thickness was estimated ... using FreeSurfer version 5.3 ... Prior to analysis, all surface reconstructions were visually assessed ... by at least 3 independent raters. We excluded a small number of scans with severe artifacts ... The rest of the scans were included 'as is' ... Cortical thickness maps were then smoothed with a 10-mm surface-based Gaussian kernel."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: Internal validation used 10-fold cross-validation on the TD cohort to assess generalization before retraining on the full TD set for predictions on ASD participants. Figures were thresholded to retain vertices accurately predicted under cross-validation.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "To assess generalization, we used 10-fold cross-validation ... before retraining the model using the whole dataset to make predictions on the ASD participants"; "only vertices that could accurately predict the true cortical thickness in the healthy cohort under cross-validation were retained"

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The study does not describe applying the normative model to an independent external healthy dataset beyond internal cross-validation. No external validation cohort of TD individuals is reported.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: No explicit application to an independent external healthy cohort is described; validation is via 10-fold cross-validation within the TD cohort.

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is well described: vertexwise Gaussian process regression with a covariance combining linear and nonlinear terms; empirical Bayes estimation; z-statistics computed per subject/vertex. However, specific implementation software/libraries for GPR are not specified.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "Gaussian process regression (GPR) was used to estimate separate normative models ... at each vertex"; "a generic covariance function combining linear and non-linear terms"; "we compute a single subject Z-statistic image for each subject ... at each brain location"

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: Model performance is assessed via cross-validation and retention of vertices with significant predictive accuracy (Pearson correlation, FDR-corrected). However, comprehensive quantitative metrics (e.g., overall R^2, error distributions) are not reported in text.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "only vertices that could accurately predict the true cortical thickness in the healthy cohort under cross-validation were retained (Pearson correlation, p < 0.05, FDR)"; "the normative model provides a good fit for [the TD cohort]. Crucially, this fit was achieved under cross-validation and is therefore unbiased."

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: Although 10-fold cross-validation is used, the sample sizes and demographics for each fold/partition are not described.
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: No per-partition (fold-level) sample sizes or demographics are provided beyond stating 10-fold cross-validation.

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Preprocessing software and version (FreeSurfer v5.3) are specified, and the data source (LEAP) is identified. However, code, trained models, and broader software environments for the GPR implementation are not specified; data access is via a consortium dataset, not openly available.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: "using FreeSurfer version 5.3"; "we included all participants from the ... LEAP cohort"; no statements found on code or trained model availability.

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: Clinical eligibility and diagnostic criteria are described (DSM-5/ICD-10). Image quality standards include visual QC and exclusion of severe artifacts, with no manual edits. Final sample size for ASD is reported (n=321). Reasons for exclusion beyond severe artifacts are not fully detailed and comorbidities/medications were not excluded by design.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "Individuals with an existing ASD and/or mild ID diagnosis (according to DSM-5/ICD-10 criteria) were recruited ... across one of seven study sites"; "Prior to analysis, all surface reconstructions were visually assessed ... We excluded a small number of scans with severe artifacts ... The rest of the scans were included 'as is' ..."; "we included ... 321 individuals ... with ASD"; "we did not exclude other comorbidities in the clinical group ... and 30-50% of individuals with ASD are on stable medications"

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses relate individual deviation scores to clinical measures including ADOS-2 and ADI-R subscores, with reported correlations (repetitive behaviors survive multiple testing). Supplementary analyses also assess associations with ADHD symptoms and IQ.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: "These deviations correlated with severity of repetitive behaviors and social communicative symptoms, although only repetitive behaviors survived corrections for multiple testing."; "we ... performed several post-hoc tests for potential confounding variables including ... comorbid ADHD symptoms"

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: The clinical cohort is drawn from the LEAP multi-site study; sites and recruitment are described.
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "we included all participants from the Longitudinal European Autism Project (LEAP) cohort ..."; "across one of seven study sites"

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: Sample sizes are reported for ASD and TD and by age/ID schedule; demographic and clinical characteristics (age, IQ, ADI-R, ADOS-2) are presented in Table 1 and Supplementary Table S1.
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: "We included 206 TD individuals ... and 321 individuals ... with ASD"; Table 1 entries for age and IQ; ADI-R and ADOS-2 scores listed; Supplementary Table S1 provides per-site characteristics.

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: Clinical measures are specified, including ADI-R and ADOS-2, along with diagnostic criteria (DSM-5/ICD-10).
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: "Individuals with an existing ASD and/or mild ID diagnosis (according to DSM-5/ICD-10 criteria)..."; "ADI-R ... Repetitive behavior ..."; "ADOS-2 ... Total ... Social ... Repetitive behavior"

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: The meaning and direction of deviations are described (negative vs positive deviations; blue indicates reduced CT and yellow increased). Thresholding for significant deviations uses intraindividual FDR. Clinical interpretation is discussed through associations with symptoms and age groups.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: "These figures show the number of participants ... that deviate negatively ... or positively ... after intraindividual FDR correction."; "Blue ... and yellow indicate reduced and increased cortical thickness, respectively."; "These deviations correlated with severity of repetitive behaviors and social communicative symptoms ... only repetitive behaviors survived corrections"; "negative deviations were most prominent in children, whereas positive deviations were most prominent in adolescents and adults"
